---
format:
  revealjs:
    theme:
      - default
      - assets/theme.scss
    width: 1600
    height: 900
    # Figure-heavy science talks that need a text column beside a large figure
    # often read better on a wider canvas. To use ~21:9, set:
    #   width: 2100
    # and scale figure base_size / linewidths up to match (see the setup chunk).
    #
    # center: false keeps content top-aligned and pins the grey data-section
    # watermark to the slide bottom edge. For content-light / card decks that
    # leave a lot of empty space below the content, set `center: true` to balance
    # each slide vertically (it uses the whole slide height instead of clustering
    # at the top). Two interactions to know before flipping it: (1) the
    # data-section watermark then sits just beneath the centred content rather
    # than the slide edge, and (2) `.absolute` bleed-figure slides and
    # `.fit-narrow` assume top-aligned slides, so re-render and re-check those.
    center: false
    slide-number: c/t
    hash: true
    menu: true
    progress: true
    controls: true
    transition: fade
    embed-resources: true
    include-after-body: assets/qa-fragments.html
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
params:
  config_file: "presentation.yml"
  project_root: "."
  install_missing_packages: true
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
# Keep embedded figures light so the self-contained HTML stays small: render
# inline figures at screen (1x) resolution. Pre-optimize any external images
# into an `optimized/` folder before embedding them (see README "File size").
# Optional sampler dependencies, named once for both installation and loading.
packages <- c(
  ggplot2 = NA,
  ggOceanMaps = NA,
  ragg = NA,
  systemfonts = NA
)
if (isTRUE(params$install_missing_packages)) {
  missing <- packages[
    !vapply(names(packages), requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
  ]
  if (length(missing)) {
    repos <- getOption("repos")
    if (is.na(repos["CRAN"]) || repos["CRAN"] == "@CRAN@") {
      repos["CRAN"] <- "https://cloud.r-project.org"
      options(repos = repos)
    }
    lib <- strsplit(Sys.getenv("R_LIBS_USER"), .Platform$path.sep)[[1]][1]
    if (!is.na(lib) && nzchar(lib)) {
      if (!dir.exists(lib)) dir.create(lib, recursive = TRUE)
      .libPaths(c(lib, .libPaths()))
    }
    options(install.packages.compile.from.source = "never")
    install.packages(names(missing))
  }
}
invisible(lapply(names(packages), function(package) {
  suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(package, character.only = TRUE))
}))

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev = "png",
  dev.args = list(bg = "transparent"),
  dpi = 96,
  fig.retina = 1
)
source("R/presentation_helpers.R")
dir.create("assets/generated", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
background_image_file <- "assets/generated/background-image.png"
grDevices::png(background_image_file, width = 1600, height = 900, bg = "#f7f8f5")
graphics::par(mar = rep(0, 4))
graphics::plot.new()
graphics::plot.window(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 1))
graphics::polygon(
  c(0, 1, 1, 0),
  c(0.00, 0.00, 0.28, 0.12),
  col = "#dcecef",
  border = NA
)
graphics::lines(
  seq(0, 1, length.out = 120),
  0.12 + 0.045 * sin(seq(0, 4 * pi, length.out = 120)),
  col = "#449bcf",
  lwd = 14
)
graphics::lines(
  seq(0, 1, length.out = 120),
  0.07 + 0.025 * cos(seq(0, 5 * pi, length.out = 120)),
  col = "#056a89",
  lwd = 7
)
grDevices::dev.off()
ggplot2::theme_set(presentation_theme())
arctic_map <- ggOceanMaps::basemap(
  60,
  bathy.style = "rbb",
  legends = FALSE,
  base_size = 18,
  land.col = "#d6dedb",
  land.border.col = "#667985",
  grid.col = "#9aa7ab"
) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.background = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
cfg <- read_presentation_config(params$config_file, params$project_root)
validate_presentation_inputs(cfg)
summary_object <- load_presentation_summary(cfg)
spict <- if (identical(cfg$data$adapter, "spict")) {
  extract_spict_context(summary_object)
} else {
  NULL
}
```

<!-- catalogue:start layout-guide -->
## The evidence type determines which slide layout is appropriate. {#layout-guide .layout-guide data-section="Authoring reference"}

| Evidence or explanation | Recommended layout | Code |
|---|---|---|
| One chart with interpretation | Text + figure | `.text-figure` |
| Dense or faceted chart | Wide figure | `.wide-figure` |
| Geographic result | Map + context | `.map-context` |
| Exact scenario values | Scenario table | `.scenario-table` |
| Concept with a representative visual | Concept + image | `.concept-image` |

::: {.notes}
This authoring reference is included in the sampler but should normally be removed from a project presentation. Select the layout from the claim and supporting evidence, then write a declarative sentence title.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end layout-guide -->

<!-- catalogue:start diagnostic-grid -->
## Four diagnostic views identify different forms of model inadequacy. {#diagnostic-grid .diagnostic-grid data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-diagnostic-grid
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.8
#| out-width: 100%
old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
graphics::par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(2.8, 3.2, 1.8, 0.8), mgp = c(1.8, 0.55, 0))
x <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 40)
graphics::plot(x, 0.12 * sin(4 * x), type = "b", pch = 19, col = "#056a89", main = "Residual structure", xlab = "Fitted value", ylab = "Residual")
graphics::abline(h = 0, col = "#9aa7ab", lty = 2)
graphics::plot(1:12, exp(-0.25 * (1:12)), type = "h", lwd = 5, col = "#449bcf", main = "Autocorrelation", xlab = "Lag", ylab = "Correlation")
graphics::plot(1:10, 1 + 0.03 * cumsum(c(-1, 1, 0, 1, -1, 0, 1, -1, 0, 1)), type = "b", pch = 19, col = "#6ca67a", main = "Retrospective stability", xlab = "Peel", ylab = "Relative estimate")
graphics::plot(c(0.9, 1.0, 1.08, 0.96), c(0.94, 1.02, 1.05, 0.99), pch = 21, bg = "#d44f56", col = "white", cex = 2.4, main = "Sensitivity", xlab = "Base estimate", ylab = "Alternative estimate")
graphics::abline(0, 1, col = "#9aa7ab", lty = 2)
graphics::par(old_par)
```

::: {.notes}
Use `.diagnostic-grid` for aligned small multiples. The figures, not explanatory cards, should occupy most of the slide. State what each diagnostic tests in the title or notes.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end diagnostic-grid -->

<!-- catalogue:start emphasis-styles -->
## Different text treatments distinguish limitations from interpretations and deadlines. {#emphasis-styles data-section="Authoring reference"}

::: {.alert-box}
Use `.alert-box` for an important limitation or risk.
:::

::: {.takeaway}
Use `.takeaway` for the interpretation that follows from the evidence.
:::

::: {.deadline}
Use `.deadline` for a review date or decision point.
:::

::: {.closing}
Use `.closing` for a short final line within a conclusion slide.
:::

::: {.notes}
These are modifiers rather than slide layouts. Apply them selectively so their distinct functions remain apparent.
:::

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.6

#| out-width: 100%

```
:::

::: {.notes}
Use `.edge-figure` for a tall or square figure that should run to the right and lower slide edges. The title and text column remain constrained; recheck the crop when the canvas ratio changes.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end edge-figure -->

<!-- catalogue:start figure-swap -->
## A fixed comparison frame makes differences between two figure variants easier to see. {#figure-swap .figure-swap data-section="Authoring reference"}

::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| label: plot-swap-a
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| out-width: 100%
plot_spict_trajectories(spict)
```
:::

::: {.fragment .fade-in fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| label: plot-swap-b
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| out-width: 100%
plot_spict_trajectories(spict)
```
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
`.figure-swap` is a fragment feature. Pair `.fade-out` and `.fade-in` on the same `fragment-index` so one figure replaces the other in exactly the same position.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end figure-swap -->

<!-- catalogue:start figure-walkthrough -->
## A figure walkthrough separates the stages of a multi-part result. {#figure-walkthrough .figure-walkthrough data-section="Results"}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="28%"}
**First** — establish the baseline.

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1}
**Then** — introduce the comparison.
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2}
**Finally** — leave the synthesis visible.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="72%"}
::: {.r-stack}
::: {.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| label: plot-seq-a
#| fig-width: 9.4
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: 100%
plot_spict_trajectories(spict)
```
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=1 .fade-in-then-out}
```{r}
#| label: plot-seq-b
#| fig-width: 9.4
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: 100%
plot_spict_trajectories(spict)
```
:::

::: {.fragment fragment-index=2 .fade-in}
```{r}
#| label: plot-seq-c
#| fig-width: 9.4
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: 100%
plot_spict_trajectories(spict)
```
:::
:::
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Synchronize each text fragment and figure with the same index. Every intermediate transparent figure must fade out before the next appears.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end figure-walkthrough -->

<!-- catalogue:start concept-image -->
## A representative figure helps the audience connect an abstract model to its observable components. {#concept-image .concept-image data-section="Explanation"}

:::: {.concept-image-grid}
::: {.concept-text}
- Observations define the empirical basis.
- The model links those observations to a latent process.
- The interpretation should refer back to what is visible in the figure.
:::

::: {.concept-visual}
```{r}
#| label: plot-concept-image
#| fig-width: 9.2
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: 100%
set.seed(8)
x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 60)
y <- 0.25 + 0.55 * x + stats::rnorm(length(x), 0, 0.055)
graphics::plot(x, y, pch = 21, bg = "#449bcf", col = "white", cex = 1.4, xlab = "Observed gradient", ylab = "Response", bty = "l")
graphics::lines(x, 0.25 + 0.55 * x, col = "#056a89", lwd = 5)
graphics::abline(h = 0.65, col = "#d44f56", lwd = 3, lty = 2)
graphics::text(0.76, 0.69, "Decision threshold", col = "#d44f56", cex = 1.2)
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Use `.concept-image` when a photograph, schematic, map, or representative scientific figure explains an unfamiliar concept. The visual should carry the mechanism or context, not serve as decoration.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end concept-image -->

<!-- catalogue:start table-figure -->
## Exact scenario values can be checked against the corresponding trend. {#table-figure .table-figure data-section="Results"}

:::: {.table-figure-grid}
::: {.table-panel .table-medium}
```{r}
#| label: table-style-sampler
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = c("Reference", "Lower catch", "Higher catch"),
    `Catch (t)` = c("TBD", "TBD", "TBD"),
    Risk = c("TBD", "TBD", "TBD"),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "r")
)
```
:::

::: {.figure-panel}
```{r}
#| label: plot-style-sampler
#| fig-width: 5.6
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| out-width: 100%
old_par <- graphics::par(no.readonly = TRUE)
graphics::par(mar = c(3.2, 3.4, 0.5, 0.5), mgp = c(2, 0.6, 0))
graphics::plot(1:6, c(2.1, 2.4, 2.2, 2.8, 3.0, 3.2), type = "b", lwd = 3, pch = 19, col = "#056a89", xlab = "Step", ylab = "Relative value", bty = "l")
graphics::par(old_par)
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Use `.table-figure` when the table provides exact values and the figure provides a compact graphical check. Remove nonessential table columns before reducing text size.

<!-- catalogue:start wide-figure -->
## Uncertainty and axis labels remain legible when the figure occupies most of the slide. {#wide-figure .wide-figure data-section="Results"}

:::: {.wide-figure-grid}
::: {.text-panel}
- Retain only the interpretation required to read the figure.
- Move detailed methods and qualifications into notes.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10.4
#| fig-height: 5.6
```

<!-- catalogue:start map-context -->
## Station distribution shows which geographic areas contribute to the estimate. {#map-context .map-context data-section="Results"}

:::: {.map-context-grid}
::: {.text-panel}
- State why the spatial coverage matters for the interpretation.
- Keep the legend and annotation brief.
:::

::: {.figure-panel}
```{r}
#| label: plot-map-context
#| fig-width: 9.6
#| fig-height: 6.4
#| out-width: 100%
stations <- data.frame(
  lon = c(-18, -5, 8, 20, 34, 12),
  lat = c(66, 71, 74, 70, 76, 81)
)
stations_projected <- ggOceanMaps::transform_coord(stations, proj.out = 3995, bind = TRUE)
arctic_map +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    data = stations_projected,
    ggplot2::aes(x = lon.proj, y = lat.proj),
    shape = 21,
    fill = "#d44f56",
    colour = "white",
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1
  )
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
Use `.map-context` for a geographic result with a short interpretation. The sampler uses bundled `rbb` bathymetry for offline rendering; `rcb` can be used when the ggOceanMaps large-data cache is available.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end map-context -->

<!-- catalogue:start full-figure -->
## The overall time-series shape is the evidence and therefore occupies the content area. {#full-figure .full-figure data-section="Results"}

```{r}
#| label: plot-full-figure
#| fig-width: 13.2
#| fig-height: 5.7
#| out-width: 100%
x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 80)
y <- 0.35 + 0.5 * x + 0.07 * sin(10 * x)
graphics::plot(x, y, type = "n", xlab = "Time", ylab = "Relative index", bty = "l")
graphics::polygon(c(x, rev(x)), c(0.29 + 0.5 * x, rev(0.41 + 0.5 * x)), col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#449bcf", 0.2), border = NA)
graphics::lines(x, y, lwd = 5, col = "#056a89")
```

::: {.small-note}
Use one brief annotation or source note only when it helps the audience read the figure.
:::

::: {.notes}
Use `.full-figure` when the figure itself carries the full assertion. Avoid overlaying callouts on data or uncertainty intervals.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end full-figure -->

<!-- catalogue:start background-image -->
## A contextual background image can support a short message without competing with it. {#background-image .background-image-slide background-image="assets/generated/background-image.png" background-size="cover" background-position="center"}

::: {.background-copy}
::: {.title-kicker}
Background image
:::

::: {.title-heading}
Use the background only when the image provides relevant context.
:::

::: {.title-subtitle}
Maintain sufficient contrast and avoid placing data-dense content over the image.
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
`background-image` is a Reveal slide attribute rather than a layout. It is appropriate for a brief contextual or section slide, not for empirical figures or tables.

<!-- catalogue:start custom-figure-font -->
## A bundled figure font keeps occasional annotations reproducible across systems. {#custom-figure-font .custom-figure-font data-section="Authoring reference"}

:::: {.text-figure-grid}
::: {.text-panel}
- Keep the font file under `assets/fonts/`.
- Register it with `systemfonts`.
- Render the figure with `ragg`.
:::

::: {.figure-panel}
```{r}
#| label: plot-custom-font
#| dev: ragg_png
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 5.2
#| out-width: 100%
family <- register_xkcd_font()
graphics::plot(c(0, 1), c(0, 1), type = "n", axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
graphics::arrows(0.16, 0.28, 0.78, 0.72, length = 0.12, lwd = 4, col = "#056a89")
graphics::text(0.48, 0.48, "Explain the change", family = family, cex = 2.1, col = "#d44f56", srt = 12)
graphics::points(0.82, 0.75, pch = 21, bg = "#6ca67a", col = "white", cex = 3, lwd = 2)
```
:::
::::

::: {.notes}
`register_xkcd_font()` and the bundled TTF are rendering features rather than a slide layout. The `ragg_png` device honours the registered font.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end custom-figure-font -->

<!-- catalogue:start table-density -->
## Named table-density modifiers preserve readable text across different column counts. {#table-density data-section="Authoring reference"}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="49%"}
### Medium table

::: {.table-medium}
```{r}
#| label: table-medium-demo
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Scenario = c("Reference", "Lower", "Upper"),
    Catch = c(780, 720, 840),
    Interpretation = c("Central case", "Lower pressure", "Higher pressure")
  ),
  align = c("l", "r", "l")
)
```
:::
:::

::: {.column width="49%"}
### Tight table

::: {.table-tight}
```{r}
#| label: table-tight-demo
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Year = 2024:2026,
    A = c(1.02, 1.04, 1.05),
    B = c(0.91, 0.95, 0.98),
    C = c(0.84, 0.88, 0.92),
    D = c(1.12, 1.09, 1.06),
    E = c(0.76, 0.79, 0.82)
  ),
  digits = 2
)
```
:::
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
`.table-medium` and `.table-tight` are modifiers. Move columns or rows to an appendix if the tight version is still difficult to read.
:::
<!-- catalogue:end table-density -->

<!-- catalogue:start scenario-table -->
## A focused scenario table supports direct comparison of the exact values. {#scenario-table .scenario-table data-section="Results"}

::: {.table-medium}
```{r}
#| label: scenario-table
knitr::kable(
  scenario_table(spict),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
)
```
:::

::: {.takeaway}
State the comparison supported by the table in one sentence.
